chunks: Spend in the way of God, and do not cast yourselves into destruction with your own hands. And do good, for indeed God loves the doers of good.

key_terms.الْمُحْسِنِينَ: the doers of good / those who excel in virtue
key_terms.سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ: the path or way of God

ai.seo_question: What does it mean to not cast oneself into destruction in Islam?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often interpreted as a comprehensive command for both material charity (Sadaqah) and spiritual self-preservation, warning against neglecting one's duties or indulging in excess that leads to ruin. The phrase 'do not throw yourselves into destruction' is linked to the concept of *Tahalluk* (ruin), emphasizing that true piety involves balancing worldly obligations with spiritual excellence (*Ihsan*), a quality highly valued in the Ahl al-Bayt's teachings.
